title: Library Imports
content: Imports `Mathlib.Analysis.Complex.Basic` for ℂ and its normed field structure, `Mathlib.Topology.MetricSpace.Basic` for metric distance, and `Mathlib.Tactic` for proof automation.
mathContext: The key Mathlib facts used are `norm_mul` (‖a·b‖ = ‖a‖·‖b‖ for normed fields), `norm_add_le` (‖a+b‖ ≤ ‖a‖+‖b‖), `Complex.norm_eq_abs` (‖z‖ = Complex.abs z), and `dist_eq_norm` (dist x y = ‖x-y‖).

title: Algebraic Identity (CommRing)
content: The identity $(z_1 - z_3)(z_2 - z_4) = (z_1 - z_2)(z_3 - z_4) + (z_2 - z_3)(z_1 - z_4)$ holds in any commutative ring. Proved by `ring` (polynomial identity checking).
mathContext: This identity is the algebraic heart of Ptolemy's theorem. It expresses the 'diagonal product' $(z_1-z_3)(z_2-z_4)$ as a sum of two 'opposite side products'. Both sides expand to the same polynomial $z_1 z_2 - z_1 z_4 - z_2 z_3 + z_3 z_4$ in the free commutative ring on four generators. The generality (any CommRing, not just $\mathbb{C}$) shows that Ptolemy is purely algebraic — the geometry enters only through the norm in the next step.

title: Specialization to ℂ
content: The algebraic identity specialized to the complex numbers ℂ. A direct instantiation of the CommRing version.
mathContext: Since $\mathbb{C}$ is a commutative ring (in fact a field), the identity holds automatically. This intermediate theorem is provided for convenience: downstream proofs can cite `ptolemy_complex_identity` without specifying the type class.

title: Ptolemy's Inequality (Main Theorem)
content: For any four complex numbers: $\|z_1 - z_3\| \cdot \|z_2 - z_4\| \leq \|z_1 - z_2\| \cdot \|z_3 - z_4\| + \|z_2 - z_3\| \cdot \|z_1 - z_4\|$. The calc proof chains four equalities/inequalities.
mathContext:
The proof proceeds:
1. $\|z_1-z_3\| \cdot \|z_2-z_4\| = \|(z_1-z_3)(z_2-z_4)\|$ by `norm_mul` (multiplicativity in normed fields)
2. $= \|(z_1-z_2)(z_3-z_4) + (z_2-z_3)(z_1-z_4)\|$ by the algebraic identity
3. $\leq \|(z_1-z_2)(z_3-z_4)\| + \|(z_2-z_3)(z_1-z_4)\|$ by `norm_add_le` (triangle inequality)
4. $= \|z_1-z_2\| \cdot \|z_3-z_4\| + \|z_2-z_3\| \cdot \|z_1-z_4\|$ by `norm_mul` again

This is arguably the shortest known proof of Ptolemy's inequality. Equality holds iff $(z_1-z_2)(z_3-z_4)$ and $(z_2-z_3)(z_1-z_4)$ have the same argument, which is equivalent to the four points being concyclic.

title: Complex.abs Formulation
content: Ptolemy's inequality restated using `Complex.abs` instead of `‖·‖`. The two agree on ℂ via `Complex.norm_eq_abs`.
mathContext: In Mathlib, `Complex.abs` is the complex absolute value (modulus) defined via `Complex.normSq`. The norm `‖z‖` on ℂ equals `Complex.abs z` by `Complex.norm_eq_abs`. This formulation may be more natural for users working with `Complex.abs` directly.

title: Distance Formulation
content: Ptolemy's inequality in metric distance form: $\text{dist}(z_1, z_3) \cdot \text{dist}(z_2, z_4) \leq \text{dist}(z_1, z_2) \cdot \text{dist}(z_3, z_4) + \text{dist}(z_2, z_3) \cdot \text{dist}(z_1, z_4)$.
mathContext: The bridge `dist_eq_norm` gives $\text{dist}(x, y) = \|x - y\|$ for normed add comm groups. This formulation connects the complex-number proof to the classical geometric statement about distances in the plane, and directly parallels the `dist`-based formulation in `PtolemysTheorem.lean`.

title: Ptolemy's Equality (Sufficient Condition)
content: If $(z_2-z_3)(z_1-z_4) = t \cdot (z_1-z_2)(z_3-z_4)$ for some real $t \geq 0$, then Ptolemy's inequality becomes equality. Both sides equal $(1+t) \cdot \|(z_1-z_2)(z_3-z_4)\|$.
mathContext: The equality case of $\|a+b\| \leq \|a\| + \|b\|$ occurs when $a$ and $b$ point in the same direction. For Ptolemy, the two 'opposite side products' $(z_1-z_2)(z_3-z_4)$ and $(z_2-z_3)(z_1-z_4)$ must be positively proportional. This condition is satisfied when the four points are concyclic in the correct ordering, as the cross-ratio is then real and positive.
